frontier_question: Why did DeepSeek's R1 release trigger the largest single-day loss in Nvidia's history, and what did it reveal about frontier-AI training economics?

chunks.content: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1, its open-weights reasoning model with accompanying paper, on 2025-01-20. Its predecessor DeepSeek-V3 (released 2024-12-26) reported training on roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about US$5.6 million, on export-restricted H800 chips. R1's reasoning was produced by reinforcement learning (GRPO), and R1-Zero was trained with no supervised fine-tuning at all. On 2025-01-27, Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization — at the time the largest single-day loss in stock-market history — with about US$1 trillion erased across the tech complex. Markets repriced the thesis that frontier-AI capex, and therefore Nvidia's demand, is moated by compute scale: an open-weights frontier-class reasoning model had been trained for a fraction of the incumbent cost. US export controls (the H800 restrictions) had forced Chinese labs toward efficiency — scarcity, not preference, drove the economics.

prior_gap_texts: DeepSeek’s R1 release triggered the largest single-day loss in Nvidia's history because it demonstrated that a frontier-class, open-weights reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of the cost previously assumed necessary [Source: ev-1].
This caused markets to reprice the thesis that demand for AI compute—and therefore Nvidia—is protected by high capital expenditure barriers and scale moats [Source: ev-1].

The event revealed several key aspects about frontier-AI training economics:
*   **Cost Efficiency:** The predecessor model, DeepSeek-V3 (released on 2024-12-26), reported training costs of approximately US$5.6 million using roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours [Source: ev-1].
R1 further advanced this efficiency through reinforcement learning (specifically GRPO) and a variant called R1-Zero which required no supervised fine-tuning at all [Source: ev-1].

*   **Impact of Export Controls:** The low-cost training was achieved partly because US export controls restricted access to high-end chips like the H800, forcing Chinese labs toward greater efficiency; scarcity drove these economic outcomes rather than mere preference [Source: ev-1].

The market reaction occurred on 2025-01-27, when Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization—the largest single-day loss in stock-market history—with about US$1 trillion erased across the tech complex overall [Source: ev-1].
DeepSeek-R1 itself had been released earlier, on 2025-1-20 [Source: ev-1].
